title: Singapore FinTech Festival Expects 20,000 Meetings. What Will Fintech Be Talking About?
description: Over 600 sponsors and exhibitors. 40+ international pavilions. Singapore FinTech Festival puts out its 11th edition at Singapore EXPO on 18 Nov.
coverAlt: Singapore FinTech Festival puts out its 11th edition at Singapore EXPO on 18 Nov.
seoTitle: Singapore FinTech EXPO Expects 20,000 Meetings. What's New?
html:
Singapore FinTech Festival is opening at Singapore EXPO on 18 November. Last year's event attracted over 70,000 participants from 142 countries, according to the Monetary Authority of Singapore. The scale is impressive, but the programme is more interesting than the attendance figures.

This year's theme is “The Coming Rewiring of the Financial System: New Risks. New Rules. New Growth.”

Behind that rather ambitious title are some very practical questions. What happens when AI agents can initiate purchases and payments? How do stablecoins fit into regulated financial services? And can cross-border payment networks become easier to connect without creating new problems for compliance and oversight? Those discussions sit alongside tokenisation, digital money and the future of financial regulation.

The event isn't limited to conference stages. Organisers are introducing a Merchant Experience area focused on how businesses buy and get paid, while the MeetUp programme is expected to arrange more than 20,000 one-to-one meetings. There are also Investor Hours for founders and investors, and an exhibition featuring AI-enabled payments, digital assets and programmable financial infrastructure. For payment providers, these are opportunities to see which ideas potential partners are prepared to discuss in commercial terms, rather than just applaud in a keynote.

One programme detail is particularly telling: the festival's agenda includes sessions on stablecoins moving into regulatory frameworks and on the commercial implications of agentic AI. Both subjects have attracted enormous attention, but a prospective merchant or financial institution will still want to know who carries the risk, how settlement works and which jurisdictions a service can support. A polished demonstration may start the conversation; those are the questions that keep it going. 

For fintech brands, conferences like SFF are also a test of positioning. If your company says it offers “the future of payments”, that won't distinguish it from hundreds of others on the exhibition floor. Explaining exactly which merchants you serve, where your infrastructure operates and what problem you solve gives business development teams something more useful to take into those meetings.

Singapore FinTech Festival runs from 18 to 20 November. We'll be watching which themes move beyond stage discussions and into partnerships, products and real commercial commitments.

About VAK Marketing

VAK Marketing is an advertising agency that has been promoting blockchain and fintech projects, crypto tokens, IT startups and Web3 ventures since 2018. The agency works with iGaming operators, platforms, PSPs and affiliate teams, as well as exchanges, wallets, DeFi and infrastructure projects in Web3, and helps founders build personal brands and visible expertise in their markets.

More at https://vakmarketing.com/.
